picks.title: Sukkot 5787: Joy in the Unknown.
picks.summary:
What if letting go of control is actually the key to joy?

In this episode, Zvi Hirschfield and Rabbi Reuven Margrett explore why Sukkot, coming on the heels of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, is called zman simchateinu—the time of our joy. They consider how the holidays form a single journey: from confronting judgment to accepting that we are not ultimately in control. The sukkah invites us to discover how that vulnerability can open the door to gratitude, closeness with God, and joy.
picks.reason: Explores Sukkot's spiritual meaning about joy, vulnerability, and divine relationship.

picks.showTitle: Entering Sukkot with Rav Shlomo Katz
picks.title: Drawing Mesirut Nefesh After Sukkot — In Memory of Ari Weiss Hy"d
picks.summary: Rav Shlomo Katz and Rabbi Stewart Weiss explore the concept of Mesirut Nefesh (self-sacrifice) during the annual memorial for Ari Weiss Hy"d, who fell in battle after Sukkot. Drawing on letters from the Lubavitcher Rebbe and teachings from the Vilna Gaon on overcoming hatred (Sinat Chinam), they redefine heroism not just as physical bravery on the battlefield, but as daily restraint, holding back in arguments, refusing to judge others, and making space in our hearts for every fellow Jew.]]>
picks.reason: Reflects on self-sacrifice and ethical restraint through Jewish teachings and memorial.

picks.title: What Actually is Religious Zionism?

What happens when a dream of redemption collides with the realities of a modern Jewish state, and what does that mean for Israel today?

picks.showTitle: Rise & Shine with Adrienne Gold Davis
picks.title: A Sukkot Lesson From a Blackout Next Door
picks.summary:
The power went out next door and stayed out for three days. My husband came home the minute it was safe to drive, found an extra-long extension cord, and ran it from our back door into our neighbors' house so their food wouldn't spoil. Nobody asked him to.
Later I told a friend about it. She isn't Jewish, and she said something I didn't expect. From everything you have taught me about Judaism, isn't that the whole point? Sharing your power and your light.
I burst into tears because she was right.
 
The Rise & Shine Podcast Series is made possible by the generous support of Bonnie Vozar of Chic
picks.reason: A personal story reflecting Jewish values of sharing and light in hardship.

picks.title: Bekhorot 5 - September 23, 12 Tishrei
picks.summary: The Gemara continues analyzing the dispute regarding whether firstborns were sanctified in the desert. According to Reish Lakish, they were not sanctified until entering the Land, whereas Rabbi Yochanan holds they were already sanctified in the wilderness. Rabbi Eleazar explains that Rabbi Yochanan derived his position from the verse "לי יהיו" ("they shall be Mine") – b'havayatan yehu, meaning that their holiness remains intact and does not lapse. Rabbi Yochanan explains the verse "והיה כי יביאך... והעברת" in accordance with the exposition of the Academy of Rabbi Yishmael: perform this mitzva
